Moose-Vehicle Collision Spatial Analysis

2020 – 2022LUKE / University of Eastern FinlandMSc thesis, September 2022

The challenge

Ungulate-vehicle collisions are an increasing safety and ecological problem across Nordic nations. In collaboration with LUKE, this project investigated how forest structure influences the spatial distribution of moose-vehicle collisions across two distinct regions of Finland: Ostrobothnia and North Karelia.

The approach

Spatial analysis mapped accident distributions by road type and season. Regression modelling tested 18 forest structure variables (canopy cover, spruce and deciduous volumes, mean heights and stem counts) against recorded collision densities. Models were built independently for each region to identify what drives the difference.

Key outcomes

  • Canopy cover and moose observation density identified as primary predictors of collision spatial variation
  • Regional differences quantified: spruce volume significant in Ostrobothnia, deciduous stems in North Karelia
  • Findings published as a thesis, available for review
